title: Why the apparent speed depends on how you watch
spoken: Apparent coordinate speed equals the model coordinate root mean square displacement divided by the observation interval.
explanation: This quotient depends on the observation interval. It is not instantaneous physical velocity. At zero interval the quotient is undefined, even though the displacement is zero.

notes.title: Define the observable
notes.explanation: This defines an interval-dependent comparison. It does not introduce a physical instantaneous Brownian velocity.

notes.title: Apparent coordinate speed
notes.explanation: A distance-per-interval statistic. It is not a molecular collision speed.

notes.title: Divide by the same interval
notes.explanation: The distance grows as the square root of time, while the denominator grows linearly. The quotient therefore decreases as the interval grows.

notes.title: Model coordinate RMS
notes.explanation: The same accepted one-coordinate model displacement used by the neighboring RMS equation.

notes.title: Positive observation interval
notes.explanation: A zero interval yields no apparent-speed value. The interface keeps the explanation instead of fabricating zero or infinity.

assumptions: The same one-coordinate ideal Brownian model as the RMS relation.
A positive observation interval is required for the quotient.
Lines joining recorded points are a rendering convention, not a velocity measurement.
